offerIntro.MainBody:
You sell data infrastructure and AI evaluation to buyers who are themselves sophisticated about technology. Government contracting officers, Fortune 500 ML leads, autonomous vehicle programs, enterprise AI teams: each needs a completely different pitch, and that is the part of enterprise GTM that nobody has time to write by hand.

So plug in your data and let agents build a page for each segment, each account, each open deal. In your brand, on your domain, rewritten as the conversation moves. That is Limitless personalization.

It built the page you are reading. Over lunch, we show your team how to do the same.

aboutIntro.MainBody:
Optimizely gives you all the tools you need to create and optimize every digital experience, with AI agents taking on the work about work. One platform, multiple use cases, trusted by 10,000+ brands.

Use-case highlight — Limitless personalization: turn your data into fully personalized pages, on brand and on your domain, that keep rewriting themselves as the account moves. The same rapid-iteration logic you apply to AI development, applied to how your marketing team reaches enterprise buyers.

aboutPillars.Title: Always yours
aboutPillars.Description: Scale AI’s brand, your tone, your messaging guidelines, your data rules. Loaded in from the start and published to your own subdomain, so every page reads like your team wrote it. In every way that counts, they did.

aboutPillars.Title: Always on
aboutPillars.Description: Pages travel the journey alongside the people on it. An account announces a new AI program, a deal moves stage, a contact opens an email or turns up at your booth — and their page already knows, and says something new.

aboutPillars.Title: Always traceable
aboutPillars.Description: Every block traces back to the signal behind it, so anyone on your team can see why a page says what it says. Nothing publishes until you allow it, and you set that rule per program.

problemThesis.Headline: Multiple verticals. Five personas each. Thousands of pages. Four steps.
problemThesis.Body:
Government buyers, Fortune 500 AI leads, autonomous vehicle programs, enterprise software teams. Every one of them needs a different page, and that has always been the part no marketing team could staff.

Now you can actually do it. Same team, same quarter, and none of it involves a design ticket or a content brief.

problemLanes.Need: Straight from your CRM, or whatever source you prefer
problemLanes.Outcome: Enterprise targets across government, autonomous vehicles, robotics, and AI software. Named contacts in open deals. Name your personas once. That is the whole brief.

problemLanes.Need: Every source you connect, every account on the list
problemLanes.Outcome: Their site, their announcements, their procurement context, your CRM history, your open deals, and the outcomes you delivered for enterprise AI teams that look just like them. Then the agents work out what matters to this one, today.

problemLanes.Need: Your brand, your domain, a live URL
problemLanes.Outcome: Written and designed inside your guidelines and published to your subdomain, ready for a seller or SDR to send. Auto-publish the ones you trust, hold review on the ones you don’t. Your call, set per programme.

A prospect announces a new AI initiative and the page picks it up. The deal moves stage and the page moves with it. No refresh project, no quarterly content audit, no Slack message to someone with a backlog.

faqs.Question: Which signals do you use?
faqs.Answer: Pick the ones you want analyzed, or let the agents surface the ones that matter to your buyer. There is no fixed list. If it lives in a system with an API, it is a variable.

faqs.Question: Does our data need to be clean first?
faqs.Answer: No. We start with what you already hold — CRM, intent data, company news, tech stack. Gaps show up in the session, and you leave knowing which ones are worth closing.

faqs.Question: Where does the copy come from?
faqs.Answer: Only from sources you approve: your site, your CRM, public filings, and news. Nothing is invented, and every block traces back to the signal behind it.

faqs.Question: Can we control what appears for a sensitive account?
faqs.Answer: Yes. Some signals shape the argument without ever appearing on the page. You decide what is visible, what only sets the tone, and what stays out entirely. Publish rules are set per programme.

faqs.Question: Do we have to move our website?
faqs.Answer: No. Pages publish on a subdomain in your brand, so your current site stays exactly as it is.

faqs.Question: Who wrote this page?
faqs.Answer: An agent did, from public signals and the same brand rules the workshop uses. That is Limitless. Connect your own systems and the pages get considerably sharper than this one.
